name: TX-30
label: Safe D

key_factors: District fundamentals are D+25 after redistricting, pointing decisively toward Democrats
Haynes holds a massive fundraising edge (~$695K vs ~$25K) plus ~$200K in outside support
Polymarket prices a Democratic win at roughly 97 percent

model.rationale: The post-redistricting fundamentals of this Dallas-area seat, a roughly 27-to-1 fundraising advantage for Haynes, and market pricing near 97 percent Democratic all align on a comfortable Democratic hold, with no evidence pointing to a competitive race.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing a single-digit race or major outside spending for Jackson would be the first sign this is closer than the fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
TX-30 is an open seat in Dallas that became more Democratic after redistricting, carrying a partisan lean of about 25 points Democratic. No general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, candidate fundraising, and market pricing. Frederick Haynes III has raised roughly $695,000 and benefits from about $200,000 in outside support, while Everett Jackson has raised about $25,000 with little cash on hand.

Prediction markets put Democratic chances near 97 percent, and the district's fundamentals point the same way. The absence of polling and expert ratings leaves some uncertainty about the exact margin, but nothing in the evidence suggests a competitive contest. The expectation is a Democratic win in the mid-twenties, consistent with the seat's strong partisan lean.
